title: Feeding behavior and morphology of mandibles in the coral reef lobster Palinurellus wieneckii (De Man, 1881) (Decapoda: Achelata: Palinuridae)
content:
Abstract
The coral reef lobster Palinurellus wieneckii (De Man, 1881) is a rare spiny lobster inhabiting coral reef caves in the Indo-West Pacific region, with little known on its feeding ecology. This study describes feeding behavior, shell damage patterns, mandible morphology, and basic information on molting frequency and growth based on long-term captive observations. Four individuals were maintained from September 2023 to May 2026 at water temperatures ranging of 24°C–27°C. Repeated observations showed that P. wieneckii used the first pereiopods to hold gastropod prey and frequently inserted the tips of the pereiopods beneath the operculum. Two distinct gastropod-shell damage patterns were recognized after predation: extensive breakage of the apical and lateral shell regions, and localized damage around the opercular opening. Logistic regression analysis indicated that the probability of shell crushing decreased significantly with increasing shell height (odds ratio = 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02–0.74, P = 0.021), with a predicted 50% crushing probability at approximately 15.1 mm shell height. The mandibles possessed broad, relatively flat occlusal surfaces and well-developed molar regions that may contribute to the processing of hard-shelled prey. All four individuals molted during captivity, with one to three molts recorded per individual and mean growth per molt of 3.3%–5.3%. These observations suggest that P. wieneckii employs two feeding strategies, shell crushing and operculum manipulation, and that its mandibles and first pereiopods play complementary roles in exploiting gastropod prey. The study provides the first detailed account of feeding behavior and associated functional morphology in this poorly known lobster.
